newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan officials visit Taiwan in payoffs probe.
newsitem.headline: Japan officials visit Taiwan in payoffs probe.

text.p: The Tokyo Grain Exchange (TGE) said on Friday that it had sent two officials to Taiwan as part of an investigation into possible payoffs by Japanese commodity brokers to favoured Taiwanese clients.

The two exchange officials, who arrived in Taiwan on Tuesday, are holding meetings with Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission and were also due to visit the Taipei branches of the five Japanese brokers, the exchange said.
"We'd like to figure out what the problem is and whether the five brokers violated any rules," Katsumi Kawamura, the TGE's senior managing director, told Reuters.
But while confirming the officials' trip to Taiwan, he declined to comment further on the status of the investigation.
The TGE and another exchange, the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM), are investigating whether the five brokers gave favourable financial treatment to some Taiwanese clients.
Industry sources have said the suspicion may be directed at red bean contracts as Taiwanese orders for the contracts listed on the TGE surged last year.

The firms, Nihon Unicom Co, Tokyo General Co, Okato Shoji Co Ltd, Kobayashi Yoko Co Ltd and International Trading Co, have not been accused of any wrongdoing. Officials contacted at the five brokers have said that they believed their operations were sound or have declined to comment.
Taiwan's SEC on Thursday confirmed that Japanese regulators had been in touch with its office but declined to say whether Taiwan officials had found any rules violations.

The grain exchange named the two senior officials visiting Taiwan as Kiyoshi Takanuma of the TGE's research division and Kunimitsu Ito of its international division. The two arrived in Taipei on March 11 and will stay for about a week.
